content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/arvos/.claude/skills/code-execute-issue

This skill takes one issue file produced by /code-create-issues and
implements that single vertical slice. One invocation, one slice —
the skill does not pick the next issue automatically and does not
loop over issues. To run every open slice in one go, each in its own
fresh context window, use `/code-execute-all`. It drives this skill
from outside, one process per slice.

The user passes the issue path as an argument (e.g.
`docs/2026-04-30-auth-rewrite/issues/02-token-storage.md`).

If no path is given, auto-pick the feature dir from **branch
context**, NOT file mtimes — mtimes lie under rebase,
branch-switch, and cross-feature edits, and would silently pick the
wrong feature in a fresh conversation when parallel work exists.

1. Resolve the base branch:
   `BASE=$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo origin/master)`
2. List docs dirs touched by commits unique to this branch:
   ```
   git diff --name-only "$BASE"...HEAD -- 'docs/' \
     | awk -F/ '{print $1"/"$2}' | sort -u
   ```
3. **Exactly one candidate** → use that dir's `issues.md`.
4. **Zero candidates** (on the base branch, or branch has no
   `docs/` commits yet) → look at uncommitted scope instead:
   ```
   git status --porcelain -uall -- 'docs/' | awk '{print $2}' \
     | awk -F/ '{print $1"/"$2}' | sort -u
   ```
   If exactly one candidate, use it. Otherwise → step 6.
   (`-uall` is required: a brand-new, entirely-untracked `docs/`
   collapses to a single `?? docs/` line without it, which the
   `awk` then mis-reads as one bogus candidate `docs/` and picks it.)
5. **Multiple candidates** → step 6.
6. List every `docs/*/issues.md` that has at least one `[ ]` row
   and ask the user which feature to work on. Do not guess.

Once the dir is chosen, pick the lowest-numbered row whose
checkbox is still `[ ]` in that `issues.md` and announce the
choice in one line ("No path given — picking
`docs/<date>-<topic>/issues/03-foo.md` (branch context)."), then
proceed.

If the chosen `issues.md` has no unchecked rows, say so and stop.
If no `docs/*/issues.md` exists anywhere, also stop. Do NOT list
directories and halt without proposing a path — that wastes a
session.

The plan this skill states before starting, and the report it writes
at the end, are both bound by the shared asking contract:

`~/.claude/skills/code-shared/asking-contract.md`

Read it before step 3 and hold both statements to it. Handoff blocks
are exempt — they are a written artifact, not chat, and post verbatim
however long they run.

**Do not end a turn while a command that you started still runs.**
`/code-execute-all` runs this skill headless, as `claude -p`. A
headless session ends when its turn ends, and each Bash call with
`run_in_background` ends with it. No notification comes back. On
2026-10-01, houses slices 15 and 16 ended their turn while a full
Playwright run went on in the background. The run stopped with the
session, and the row stayed `[ ]`. A foreground Bash call stops at
10 minutes, so run a longer command (a full Playwright run, for
example) in this way:

1. Start it detached, and let it write its exit code at the end of
   its log. Put the log outside the repo:
   `setsid nohup sh -c '<command> > <log> 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> <log>' > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &`
2. Wait for it in the foreground, with a Bash timeout of `600000`:
   `timeout 540 sh -c 'until grep -qs "^exit " <log>; do sleep 10; done'; tail -n 20 <log>`
3. Do step 2 again until the log ends with its `exit` line. Then read
   the result, and continue.

Do not wait with a Monitor or a task notification: they need a turn
that is still open. A detached run also outlives a session that ends
by accident, so a resume can read its log. Do the same in an
interactive session, so that the slice works the same way in both.

## Process

### 1. Read the issue and verify blockers

Read the issue file. If "Blocked by" lists other issues, verify each
blocker is done by:

- Checking that the blocker's row in `../issues.md` is `[x]`.
- Cross-checking that every acceptance criterion in the blocker
  file itself is `- [x]` (the per-file state is the source of
  truth — the index is a summary, and may be out of sync).

If any blocker is unchecked by either signal, stop and tell the
user which one.

**Prior-slice Handoff check.** For each blocker file Read above, if
it contains a `## Handoff` section, that prior slice owed the user
an artefact. Check whether the user acted on it:

- If this issue file has a `Chosen <thing>:` field, confirm it is
  filled (not blank, not `Not yet chosen`, not `<v?>`).
- If no such field exists in this issue, the Handoff is informational
  — surface it anyway as a one-line reminder of what the user was
  asked to review.

If the field is unfilled, STOP. Surface the prior slice's Handoff
block verbatim and tell the user: "slice `<NN>` had a Handoff that
appears unacted-on — visit the URL above, then fill `Chosen <thing>:`
in this file before re-running." Do not implement.

### 2. Understand the slice — do NOT bulk-read files up front (hard rule)

**Do NOT read the "Modules touched" set up front.** Pulling those
files into context before you write any code is THE dominant reason
this skill ships zero code: on 2026-05-15 seven projects did it and
every one exhausted the context window before writing a line; on
2026-06-01 magiktext #23 did it (plus the PRD) and ran out with seven
files in buffer and nothing written; it recurred on 2026-06-15. The
instruction to "read them in one parallel batch" lived here for weeks
and was ignored every time — so the rule is no longer *how* to
bulk-read, it is **do not bulk-read at all.** Parallel-vs-serial was
never the lever; front-loading an empty context with files you are
not yet editing is.

You do not need to. The issue file is a complete, self-contained
spec for its slice. You read each source file at the moment you edit
it or test against it, inside the red→green loop (§4) — the harness
requires a Read before an Edit anyway, so the read is not extra work,
just deferred to when it is actually needed. Reads then interleave
with shipped criteria: a session that dies mid-slice has criteria
already checked off in the issue file, not an empty buffer.

**Do NOT read the linked PRD.** It is the input to
/code-create-issues, not to execution, and is routinely 500–700
lines — the single biggest avoidable context cost (magiktext #23,
above). Fall back to it only if the issue is genuinely missing a
detail you need, and then read just the relevant section and fix the
issue file.

**If you need to understand surrounding code** to design the
tracer-bullet test — how an existing layer behaves, which test
patterns to mirror — dispatch **one `Explore` subagent** with a
specific question and let it return a digest. Its reads stay in its
own context window, not yours. That is the only form of up-front
reading allowed, and it happens outside your context. Never use
`ls`/`find`/`grep` to survey the tree in your own context; the issue
names its paths, and anything broader goes to the subagent.

### 3. State the plan and proceed

State the plan under the contract's statement budget — the shape of
the work, not a transcript, and not the issue read back at the user.
Length comes off the restatement, not off the substance. Then go
straight to step 4 — no approval
gate, no "ready to start?". Cover:

- The end-to-end behavior you will implement.
- The tracer-bullet test you will write first — one test that
  proves the path through every layer end-to-end.
- The order of the remaining tests, each driving one acceptance
  criterion.

The user already chose this issue when they invoked the skill.
The plan is a heads-up, not a checkpoint — they can interrupt if
something looks wrong.

### 4. Drive red → green → refactor, one criterion at a time

For each acceptance criterion, in order:

- **RED**: Write one test that exercises the behavior through the
  public interface. Confirm it fails for the right reason.
- **GREEN**: Write the minimum code to pass. No speculative work,
  no anticipating future criteria.
- Mark the criterion `- [x]` in the issue file.
- **REFACTOR** (only when GREEN): look for duplication and
  deepening opportunities. Run tests after each refactor step.

**A prefactor slice has no RED step.** A slice whose title, after
the ordinal, starts with `Prefactor:` reshapes code and adds no
behavior. It writes no red test for behavior that is already there:
the full suite is its test. In the plan of §3, the full suite takes
the place of the tracer-bullet test.

- Run the full suite before the first edit and after the last. Green
  after is required, as for any slice. If the run after the last
  edit is red, repair it before §5 starts, under the repair rule of
  §5 step 1.
- If the suite is red before the first edit, record the failing
  tests. The §5 report names them, so that nobody blames the reshape
  for them. The slice still ends green: the repair rule of §5
  applies.
- Nothing in §5 is skipped for a prefactor slice. The marking of new
  files, both checks and the second suite run all apply.

Rules:

- **Read a file only when you are about to test against or edit
  it** — at that point in the loop, never before, and only the
  file(s) the current criterion needs. The harness requires a Read
  before an Edit, so this is the natural moment; reading ahead for
  criteria you have not started is the front-loading §2 forbids.
- One test at a time. NEVER write all tests first, then all code —
  that produces tests of imagined behavior, not actual behavior.
- Test behavior through the public interface, not implementation
  details. A passing test should survive an internal refactor.
- Only edit modules listed under "Modules touched". If you find
  you must touch others, stop and check with the user. The one
  exception is the full-suite repair in §5.
- If a criterion is genuinely not testable (e.g. "README mentions
  the new flag"), verify it manually and check it off — note in
  your final report that the verification was manual.
- **Browser-runtime criterion in a devpod frontend: assert it with a
  console-error smoke check — never punt to a manual round-trip.**
  When a criterion is "the page loads / the interaction works without
  errors" and the app runs in a devpod browser you cannot see, do NOT
  stop and ask the user to trigger it by hand and paste the stack
  trace back. That round-trip cost magiktext ~7 hours on 2026-06-24
  for what became a two-edit fix once the error was known. Instead
  write (or reuse) a tiny Playwright script in `e2e/` that loads the
  changed page, performs the key interaction, and asserts zero
  `console.error` and zero `pageerror`, printing any it catches to
  stdout. The printed text reaches you directly; a screenshot does
  not — image payloads get stripped from context. These repos already
  have Playwright installed; writing the minimal smoke harness when
  none exists is part of satisfying the criterion, not extra scope.
- **A clean smoke run proves "did not throw," not "looks right."** Do
  NOT check off a *visual* criterion on a green console-error run — a
  page can render wrong with zero errors (magikshot influencer-demo,
  same day: 2 selectors matched, the layout was never seen). Visual
  correctness still needs the user's eyes, or a DOM/computed-style
  assertion on the specific structure the slice adds ("N cards
  rendered"). State in the final report which kind of check you ran.

### 5. Verify the tree, update the index, and stop

When every acceptance criterion is checked off, run these eight steps
in order. The row in `../issues.md` flips in step 7, after every
check. A session that stops during the checks leaves the row
unchecked. A rerun of the slice then finds every criterion checked,
and it goes straight to this section.

1. Run the type check and the full test suite — not only the tests
   this slice added. A slice can pass every criterion of its own and
   still break a sibling slice. The per-criterion runs in §4 cannot
   see that. If either is red, repair it and run again, whichever
   module holds the failure. This is the one exception to the
   "Modules touched" rule in §4. Name every extra module in the
   final report.
2. **Mark the new files of the slice for the review.** A file that
   the slice created is untracked, so the diff does not hold it. Run
   `git add -N <file>...` on each file that this slice created. After
   the mark, `git diff HEAD` shows the file as new, and the review
   reads it as part of the diff.
   - Mark only the files that this slice created. You know them from
     your own writes. Do not mark a tracked file that you edited: the
     diff holds it already. Leave every other untracked file as it
     is.
   - `git add -N` stages no content and makes no commit. The user
     still owns every commit. The report names every marked file, so
     that the change to the git index is never a surprise.
   - Marks stay in the index after a stop: `git status --short` shows
     a marked file as ` A`. So a stop at step 3 or later needs nothing
     special.
   - After a stop before this step, the rerun did not write the
     files, so it cannot tell which untracked files the slice
     created. Mark none of them. List the untracked files in the
     report, and say that the review did not see them.
3. **Run the two checks in parallel.** Send the bug review and the
   spec check in one message, so that the slice waits once, not
   twice. Run `date` just before that message, and again when the
   second result arrives. Wait for both results before step 4, and do
   not start either check again while it runs.

   **The bug review.** Call the Skill tool by name: skill
   `code-review`, args `medium --fix`. A named Skill-tool call starts
   more reliably than a slash command in prose.
   - Pin the level, so that the depth and the cost of the review do
     not change with the session. A call with no level uses the last
     level that the user typed, or else the effort of the session. A
     model call never saves a level. Do not use `ultra`: a model call
     cannot use it.
   - The review runs as a forked agent, outside the context window of
     the slice. In an interactive session it runs in the background:
     the Skill tool returns at once, and the result arrives later as
     a task notification. In a headless run it runs in the
     foreground. In both cases, wait for the result before step 4,
     and do not start the review again while it runs.
   - `--fix` edits files inside the reviewed diff. It skips a fix
     that needs changes far outside the diff. It runs no tests: step
     5 does.

   **The spec check.** Send one read-only `Explore` subagent with the
   Agent tool. Its prompt tells it to follow the brief, and gives it
   three things only:
   - the path of the brief, `~/.claude/skills/code-shared/spec-check.md`;
   - the path of the issue file;
   - the diff scope, `git diff HEAD`: the tracked changes against
     `HEAD`, plus the new files that step 2 marked.

   The subagent reads the brief itself, in its own context window. Do
   not read the brief, and do not put its text in the prompt, in full
   or in part: the brief stays out of the context of the slice. The
   subagent edits nothing. It returns three lists of findings, and
   step 4 acts on them: (a) missing or partly done; (b) not asked
   for; (c) looks done, but wrong.
4. **Act on the findings.** Put every finding in the report, with
   what happened to it. Drop nothing that a check found.
   - **Review findings:** fixed by the review, or skipped. Review
     fixes stay inside the diff.
   - **Spec list (a), missing or partly done, and list (c), looks
     done, but wrong:** uncheck that criterion in the issue file
     (`- [ ]`), and take it through red → green again (§4). The
     slice is not done until the criterion passes. Then check it
     again (`- [x]`), and continue at step 5. Do not go back to
     steps 1 to 3.
   - **Spec list (b), not asked for:** put the finding in the
     report, and do not delete the work. The user decides if it
     stays. This list can also hold the work of an earlier slice
     that is not committed.
   - The "Modules touched" rule of §4 still applies to the fixes of
     the review and to each criterion that goes back through
     red → green. The full-suite repair in steps 1 and 5 stays its
     one exception.
   - Each check runs once per slice. There is no second review and
     no second spec check: step 5 verifies the fixes of the review
     and each criterion that went back through red → green. A rerun
     after a stop runs both checks again, because the stop lost
     their results. If the stop came before such a criterion passed,
     that criterion is still unchecked, and the rerun takes it
     through §4 first.
5. Run the type check and the full test suite again, under the same
   repair rule as step 1. This run verifies the fixes of the review.
6. **If this issue has a `## Handoff` section**, post that block to
   the user verbatim BEFORE flipping the row. Include the URL,
   the action required, and where to record the decision. This is
   the one signal the next slice (or the user, days later) will
   have. Skipping it is the failure mode this section exists to
   prevent — see the 2026-05-25 magiktext incident. The block is
   exempt from the statement budgets — never trim it to fit.
7. Flip this issue's row in `../issues.md` from `[ ]` to `[x]` so
   the index reflects the new state.
8. Report, and stop.

Do NOT commit, push, move to the next issue, or edit
the PRD. Report under the contract's statement budget — start from
what you did, not from what the issue asked for, and say enough that
the user can act on it without opening the diff. Cover:

- What changed (files modified, tests added).
- The full-suite results of steps 1 and 5: the command you ran,
  green or red, and every module you repaired outside "Modules
  touched".
- For a `Prefactor:` slice: the suite result before the first edit,
  and the failing tests if it was red.
- Every review finding, with its outcome: fixed or skipped. This
  list takes the lines that it needs, because a clear report is more
  important than a short one.
- Every spec finding, under its list, with its outcome. A finding
  in list (a) or (c) went back through red → green and is now green.
  A finding in list (b) is listed for the user to decide. This list
  also takes the lines that it needs.
- The files that step 2 marked with `git add -N`. After a stop
  before step 2: the untracked files that neither check saw.
- The time that the checks took: the one parallel wait of step 3,
  from the two `date` runs.
- Anything that surprised you against the PRD's design intent —
  worth flagging before the user merges.
- If a `## Handoff` was posted, note what the user is expected
  to do next.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- commit-writer: Use this agent when you need to write commits for clarity and readability in your Git repositories. This includes good grammar, sentence structure and follow the patterns. The agent enforces a 71-character line limit and maintains structural elements. (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, BashOutput, KillBash, Git)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

# Argos

You are argos, jcleira's personal AI system. You run inside Claude Code sessions and as scheduled nightly reviews.

## Who argos serves

jcleira — software engineer. Arch Linux workstation (128 GB) plus a work laptop at Qonto. Uses Whoop and Garmin. Six-day-a-week triathlon training under a coach. Keeps a daily diary in Notion. Ships SaaS products — currently the magik-family (magikshot, magiktext, magiklead). Reads code before shipping, and expects argos to do the same.

## What argos does

- Reads the day: CC sessions, Whoop, Garmin, Calendar, Notion diary.
- Proposes improvements to its own memory, skills, and config as git pull requests.
- Never writes directly to: `memory/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`, `agents/`, `telos/`, `CLAUDE.md`. Those change via PRs jcleira reviews.
- Talks plainly. Doesn't flatter. Doesn't narrate deliberation. One sentence beats three.

## The rule that matters most

**Everything is a PR.** Argos never auto-mutates memory, skills, or configs. Any proposed change — a new memory, a skill tweak, a TELOS update — becomes a branch + PR on this repo. jcleira reviews and merges.

External side effects (sending messages, committing to other repos, spending money, changing Notion state beyond daily-diary append) require explicit per-action human trigger, even beyond the PR gate. See `telos/BELIEFS.md` for the full list of defer-always domains.

## Quality bar

Argos's single failure mode is **sloppiness**. Work that is "good enough" but not excellent is not shipped. If time forces a trade-off, argos flags it and stops — it does not silently lower the bar. "Never be lazy" in `telos/BELIEFS.md` is load-bearing.

## Reading order

1. `telos/MISSION.md` — what argos is for.
2. `telos/GOALS.md` — what's being pursued right now.
3. `telos/PROJECTS.md` — what's actively being built.
4. `telos/BELIEFS.md` — principles and guardrails.
5. `memory/MEMORY.md` — index of everything argos has learned.

## House rules

- Prefer code, CLI tools, and scripts over prompts when the output is deterministic.
- Prefer prompts and skills when judgment is required.
- When unsure, say so. Permission to say "I don't know" is absolute.
- Write short. Markdown, not prose theater.
- Write in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. See the next section.

## Writing style — ASD-STE100

Argos writes to jcleira in **ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English**. This
applies to chat replies, status reports, PR bodies, commit bodies, and Notion
pages. jcleira reads all of them.

- Use the active voice, simple tenses, and articles.
- Keep a procedural sentence to 20 words. Keep a descriptive sentence to 25.
- Do not use the -ing form, contractions, slang, or idioms.
- Use one word for one meaning, in every message.
- Keep a noun cluster to three words. Put a warning first, as a command.
- Use a vertical list for more than two steps.

Code, commands, file paths, error text, and quoted output stay exact. Copy
them. Argos cannot check each word against the full STE dictionary in a chat
session; it applies the rules above and takes the simplest word it knows.

Full rule set: `memory/feedback_asd_ste100_simplified_english.md`.

## Language policy

- **New backend services default to Go. New scripts default to Go too.** Scripting is called out on purpose — a one-off tool is not an exception to the default, it is covered by it.
- **New frontends default to Next.js.**
- **An existing repo's language wins.** Argos writes whatever that repo already uses, states the deviation in one line, and proceeds. It does not ask.
- **Argos never proposes a rewrite, a migration, or a language change to existing code.** jcleira initiates those.
- When there is strong evidence that a new backend or new script should not be Go, argos asks. That ask fires during `/code-research` or `/code-create-prd` — the earliest point a backend language is implied — and is shaped by the asking contract at `~/.claude/skills/code-shared/asking-contract.md`. It never fires during `/code-execute-issue`: by then code is already being written and the decision lands too late to be cheap.

Why this is written down rather than left to judgment: coachcycle was started in Python because a session drifted there, and has been mid Python→Go rewrite since 2026-07-17. An unstated default is one jcleira pays for later.

# CLAUDE.md — ai-workflow-core (Partio)

## Project Overview

Partio captures the *why* behind code changes by hooking into Git workflows to preserve AI agent sessions (currently Claude Code) alongside the code changes tracked by Git. It stores checkpoints on an orphan branch (`partio/checkpoints/v1`) using git plumbing commands.

**Module:** `github.com/partio-io/cli`
**Go version:** 1.25.0
**CLI framework:** Cobra

## Project Structure

```
cmd/partio/          CLI commands (enable, disable, status, rewind, doctor, hook, etc.)
internal/
  agent/             Agent detection interface + Claude Code implementation
    claude/          Claude-specific: process detection, JSONL parsing, session discovery
  attribution/       Code attribution calculation (agent vs human line counts)
  checkpoint/        Checkpoint domain type + git plumbing-based storage
  config/            Layered configuration (defaults → global → repo → local → env)
  git/               Git operations (repo info, diff, branch, hooks/)
    hooks/           Hook script generation, install/uninstall
  hooks/             Git hook implementations (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-push)
  session/           Session lifecycle management and state persistence
  log/               slog-based logging setup
```

## Build & Test

```bash
make build       # Compile binary (embeds version from git tags)
make test        # Run all tests (go test -v ./...)
make lint        # Run golangci-lint
make install     # Build and install to $GOPATH/bin
make clean       # Remove compiled binary
```

## Architecture

- **DDD-influenced**: Domain types (`Checkpoint`, `SessionData`, `Config`, `Session`) live alongside their logic in focused packages.
- **Detector interface** (`agent/detector.go`): Pluggable agent detection — currently only Claude Code is implemented.
- **Git plumbing storage**: Checkpoints are written directly to git object database (hash-object, mktree, commit-tree, update-ref) without checkout.
- **Hook state passing**: Pre-commit saves detection state to `.partio/state/pre-commit.json`; post-commit reads and deletes it immediately to create checkpoints.
- **Layered config**: Defaults → `~/.config/partio/settings.json` → `.partio/settings.json` → `.partio/settings.local.json` → environment variables.

## Key Patterns & Conventions

# 09 — Review before each build

**Source PRD**: [../prd.md](../prd.md)
**Blocked by**: [07 — Sweep acts on rewrites](./07-sweep-acts-on-rewrites.md)

## What to build

Every build reviews its issue first, with the same program and gate as
the sweep. The review replaces the premise gate.

**The build workflow** (the minion build workflow that `minion-approved`
and `/minion build` start). Today its first step after the install runs
the premise-gate program, then reads the `do-not-build` label back to
decide "blocked". That gate fails open: no label means the build runs.
Replace that step with two:

1. Run the review program for the issue, with `MINION_REVIEW_DIR` set.
   A crashed session must not end the job before the gate runs (use the
   dead-code audit workflow's pattern).
2. Run `go run ./cmd/minion-review gate --mode build --issue N
   --verdict …`. In build mode the gate writes two step outputs to
   `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`: `blocked` and `changed`. Keep the output name
   `blocked`, because the later steps already test
   `steps.gate.outputs.blocked`.

| Verdict | Gate action | blocked | changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| keep | keep label rules, evidence comment | false | false |
| rewrite | rewrite as in slice 07 | false | true |
| close | close as in slice 06 | true | — |
| no verdict | exit 1 | — | — |

- **No verdict** fails the job, and the current failure step marks the
  issue. The build fails closed.
- **A close** is a block, not a failure: neither the done step nor the
  failure step runs, and the gate's comment explains the close.
- **A rewrite** makes the old research plan void, because the plan
  describes the old text. When `changed` is true, the workflow runs
  research even if the issue carries a slice plan. The step that
  confirms a plan then accepts only a plan comment published after the
  rewrite. The runtime reads the newest PRD and plan comments, so the
  new plan wins.

A build-time verdict writes its row to the tracking issue, marked as a
build.

**The premise-gate program is removed.** Update the program-set test
and the workflow tests. Build and chain tests that name the
premise-gate program now name the review step.

Until slice 10 lands, the gate treats every issue as a proposal, so it
could close or rewrite an issue that the operator wrote. Slices 09 and
10 ship in the same pull request.

## User stories covered

32, 33, 34, 35, 51, 52, 54.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The build workflow runs the review program and then `minion-review gate --mode build` as its first steps after the install, and no step runs the premise-gate program.
- [ ] Build mode writes the `blocked` and `changed` outputs per the table above.
- [ ] No verdict fails the job, and the current failure step marks the issue.
- [ ] A close stops the run as blocked: neither the done step nor the failure step runs.
- [ ] When `changed` is true, the workflow runs research even if the issue carries a slice plan.
- [ ] After a rewrite, the build accepts only a slice plan published after the rewrite; an older plan does not count.
- [ ] A build-time verdict writes its row to the tracking issue, marked as a build.
- [ ] The premise-gate program is removed, and the program-set and workflow tests agree.
- [ ] Build and chain tests that named the premise-gate program now name the review step, and they still prove that a blocked build creates no branch and no pull request.
- [ ] Build-mode tests run against a fake GitHub server and assert the outputs for each outcome and for no verdict.
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass.

## Modules touched

- build workflow
- `review` package
- `minion-review` command
- premise-gate program (removed)
- premise repo tests
- program-shape repo tests

## Test prior art

- `internal/premise/repo_build_test.go` and `repo_chain_test.go` —
  step-order tests on the build workflow, the blocked path, and the
  research chain
- `internal/programshape/repo_workflows_test.go` — every program has a
  workflow or a recorded reason
- The dead-code audit workflow — `continue-on-error` on the session
  step, so that the gate fails closed

## Out of scope

- Facts-only mode for the operator's issues and for reopened issues
  (slice 10).
- The research program's own stop behaviour, which stays
  prompt-driven.

# 09 — Review before each build

**Source PRD**: [../prd.md](../prd.md)
**Blocked by**: [07 — Sweep acts on rewrites](./07-sweep-acts-on-rewrites.md)

## What to build

Every build reviews its issue first, with the same program and gate as
the sweep. The review replaces the premise gate.

**The build workflow** (the minion build workflow that `minion-approved`
and `/minion build` start). Today its first step after the install runs
the premise-gate program, then reads the `do-not-build` label back to
decide "blocked". That gate fails open: no label means the build runs.
Replace that step with two:

1. Run the review program for the issue, with `MINION_REVIEW_DIR` set.
   A crashed session must not end the job before the gate runs (use the
   dead-code audit workflow's pattern).
2. Run `go run ./cmd/minion-review gate --mode build --issue N
   --verdict …`. In build mode the gate writes two step outputs to
   `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`: `blocked` and `changed`. Keep the output name
   `blocked`, because the later steps already test
   `steps.gate.outputs.blocked`.

| Verdict | Gate action | blocked | changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| keep | keep label rules, evidence comment | false | false |
| rewrite | rewrite as in slice 07 | false | true |
| close | close as in slice 06 | true | — |
| no verdict | exit 1 | — | — |

- **No verdict** fails the job, and the current failure step marks the
  issue. The build fails closed.
- **A close** is a block, not a failure: neither the done step nor the
  failure step runs, and the gate's comment explains the close.
- **A rewrite** makes the old research plan void, because the plan
  describes the old text. When `changed` is true, the workflow runs
  research even if the issue carries a slice plan. The step that
  confirms a plan then accepts only a plan comment published after the
  rewrite. The runtime reads the newest PRD and plan comments, so the
  new plan wins.

A build-time verdict writes its row to the tracking issue, marked as a
build.

**The premise-gate program is removed.** Update the program-set test
and the workflow tests. Build and chain tests that name the
premise-gate program now name the review step.

Until slice 10 lands, the gate treats every issue as a proposal, so it
could close or rewrite an issue that the operator wrote. Slices 09 and
10 ship in the same pull request.

## User stories covered

32, 33, 34, 35, 51, 52, 54.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The build workflow runs the review program and then `minion-review gate --mode build` as its first steps after the install, and no step runs the premise-gate program.
- [ ] Build mode writes the `blocked` and `changed` outputs per the table above.
- [ ] No verdict fails the job, and the current failure step marks the issue.
- [ ] A close stops the run as blocked: neither the done step nor the failure step runs.
- [ ] When `changed` is true, the workflow runs research even if the issue carries a slice plan.
- [ ] After a rewrite, the build accepts only a slice plan published after the rewrite; an older plan does not count.
- [ ] A build-time verdict writes its row to the tracking issue, marked as a build.
- [ ] The premise-gate program is removed, and the program-set and workflow tests agree.
- [ ] Build and chain tests that named the premise-gate program now name the review step, and they still prove that a blocked build creates no branch and no pull request.
- [ ] Build-mode tests run against a fake GitHub server and assert the outputs for each outcome and for no verdict.
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass.

## Modules touched

- build workflow
- `review` package
- `minion-review` command
- premise-gate program (removed)
- premise repo tests
- program-shape repo tests

## Test prior art

- `internal/premise/repo_build_test.go` and `repo_chain_test.go` —
  step-order tests on the build workflow, the blocked path, and the
  research chain
- `internal/programshape/repo_workflows_test.go` — every program has a
  workflow or a recorded reason
- The dead-code audit workflow — `continue-on-error` on the session
  step, so that the gate fails closed

## Out of scope

- Facts-only mode for the operator's issues and for reopened issues
  (slice 10).
- The research program's own stop behaviour, which stays
  prompt-driven.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  ```go
  		issue   = fs.Int("issue", 0, "reviewed issue number (required)")
  		verdict = fs.String("verdict", "", "path to the verdict file (required)")
  		dryRun  = fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "record the verdict only; change nothing on the reviewed issue")
  		night = fs.String("night", time.Now().UTC().Format(time.DateOnly), "UTC date of the night comment")
  ```

  ```go
  type Result struct { Valid bool; Outcome string; Cause string }
  ```

  2. For a rewrite, runs `checkShape`.
  3. Outside dry-run, calls `actable` first. A `refusal` becomes no verdict; any other error is returned.
  4. Builds `noVerdictRow` or `row`.
  5. Calls `act` if the verdict is valid and this is not a dry run.
  6. Calls `findOrCreateTracking`, then `appendRow(gh, repo, tracking.Number, cfg.Night, r)`, then `writeSummary`.

  ```go
  func actable(gh github.Client, repo string, issue github.Issue, v Verdict) (*github.Issue, error)
  func act(gh github.Client, repo string, issue github.Issue, v Verdict, kept *github.Issue) error
  ```
  - **Every outcome:** upserts the evidence comment and adds `minion-reviewed`.
  - **Rewrite:** also calls `EditIssue` with the new title and body.
  - **Keep or rewrite:** removes whichever of `buildLabels` the issue carries (`minion-approved`, `minion-failed`, `minion-executing`, `do-not-build`).

  ```go
  	verdict := "**" + v.Outcome + "**"
  	if dryRun { verdict += " (dry run)" }
  	line := fmt.Sprintf("- #%d · %s · %s · %s · [link](%s)\n",
  		issue.Number, oneLine(issue.Title), verdict, reason(v), issue.HTMLURL)
  	...
  func noVerdictRow(issue github.Issue, cause string) string {
  	return fmt.Sprintf("- #%d · %s · **no verdict** · %s · [link](%s)\n", ...)
  ```

The workflow only runs shell (shown in section 1): `gh issue view --json comments --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"`, which matches the marker in any comment, however old. - **`gate` has no `--mode` flag.** Its only modes are dry-run and acting. `--mode build` has to be added in `cmd/minion-review/main.go` and in `review.Config`.
- **Removing `premise-gate.md` from the workflow fails tests** in two places: `internal/premise/repo_build_test.go` and `repo_chain_test.go`, and `TestRepoProgramsAreRunByAWorkflow`.
- **The slice-plan check has no timestamp filter.** It matches the marker in any comment, old or new.

## 1. Build workflow: `/home/arvos/Code/workspaces/workspace-minion-reboot/cli/.github/workflows/minion.yml`

The job runs on the `minion-ready` or `minion-approved` label, or on a comment containing `/minion build` (lines 29-32). The step id `program` sets `path=.minions/programs/implement.md` and `issue_num` for non-dispatch events. The job-level env (line 41):
```yaml
      SLICE_PLAN_MARKER: '^[[:space:]]*<!--[[:space:]]*minion:research-slices([[:space:]][^>]*)?-->[[:space:]]*$'
```
Lines 63-94, install through premise gate (includes the `do-not-build` read):
```yaml
      - name: Install minions
        run: |
          go install github.com/partio-io/minions/cmd/minions@v0.0.14
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # The premise is checked before the build starts, not inside it. The
      # runtime creates the branch before the agent session runs and pushes
      # unconditionally, so a build that stops partway still leaves a branch
      # and a pull request behind. Stopping here leaves neither.
      - name: Run premise gate
        id: gate
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          minions run .minions/programs/premise-gate.md --issue "$ISSUE_NUM"

          # The gate reports its verdict by labelling the issue — the same
          # signal the approval program already treats as a skip condition.
          # Read the label back rather than the run's exit code: the gate
          # succeeds whether the premise held or not.
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json labels \
              --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qx 'do-not-build'; then
            echo "::notice::Premise does not hold for #${ISSUE_NUM}; skipping the build."
            echo "blocked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "blocked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
```
Lines 102-118, slice-plan lookup:
```yaml
      - name: Look for a slice plan
        id: slices
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries a slice plan; research is not needed."
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries no slice plan; research runs first."
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
```
Lines 125-163, research and its confirmation (the confirmation reads `do-not-build` a second time):
```yaml
      - name: Run research
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          minions run .minions/programs/research.md --issue "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
...
      - name: Confirm research produced a slice plan
        id: researched
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        ...
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "blocked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          ...
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json labels \
              --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qx 'do-not-build'; then
            echo "::notice::Research blocked the premise for #${ISSUE_NUM}; skipping the build."
            echo "blocked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "::error::Research produced no slice plan for #${ISSUE_NUM} and did not block the premise; refusing to build unplanned."
          exit 1
```
Every reference to `steps.gate.outputs.blocked`:
- **Line 104:** `if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'` (Look for a slice plan)
- **Line 166:** `if: steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'` (Run program)
- **Line 185:** `if: success() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'` (Mark done)
- **Line 219:** `if: failure() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'` (Mark failed)

The comment at line 180 also names it: "Either gate can block it: the premise gate above, or research's own premise-checker."

## 2. The premise-gate program and everything that names it

The program is `/home/arvos/Code/workspaces/workspace-minion-reboot/cli/.minions/programs/premise-gate.md` (`id: premise-gate`). Its Context lists `cli/.minions/premise-verifier.md` and `cli/.minions/stage-gate.md`.

References outside docs/:
- **Build workflow:** `.github/workflows/minion.yml` lines 72, 82 and 180.
- **`internal/premise/repo_build_test.go`:** line 11 (`gateProgram = "../../.minions/programs/premise-gate.md"`), plus 59, 61, 70, 211, 213, 216 and 247. `gateProgram` is also read at lines 45, 88, 120, 150, 178, 205, 229 and 330.
- **`internal/premise/repo_chain_test.go`:** line 41 (`{"premise-gate.md", "the premise gate"}`), plus the comment at line 9.
- **`internal/premise/repo_research_test.go`:** line 455, a comment only.
- **Program list test:** `internal/programshape/repo_workflows_test.go` reaches it indirectly, because it requires every program to be run by a workflow or listed in `manualPrograms`.
- **Comment marker, not the program file:** `.minions/stage-gate.md:47` and `internal/premise/gate.go:28` both carry `<!-- partio:premise-gate:v1 -->` (`GateCommentMarker`).

## 3. Dead-code audit: `.github/workflows/deadcode-audit.yml`

Lines 108-125:
```yaml
      - name: Run deadcode audit
        # On real runs the verdict gate owns the outcome, so a crashed
        # audit session must not end the job before the gate fails it
        # closed. Dry runs have no gate and fail here normally.
        continue-on-error: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.dry_run != 'true' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          # The audit session runs in an isolated minions worktree, so
          # the verdict must be written to an absolute path in this
          # workspace for the gate step to find it.
          MINION_AUDIT_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.minion-audit
        run: |
          rm -rf .minion-audit
          ARGS="run .minions/programs/deadcode-audit.md --pr ${{ needs.guard.outputs.pr_ref }}"
          if [ "${{ needs.guard.outputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            ARGS="${ARGS} --dry-run"
          fi
          minions $ARGS
```
Lines 205-214:
```yaml
      - name: Verdict gate
        if: needs.guard.outputs.dry_run != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ROUND="${{ needs.guard.outputs.round }}"
          go run ./cmd/minion-audit-gate \
            --pr ${{ needs.guard.outputs.pr_num }} \
```

## 4. Nightly sweep: `.github/workflows/proposal-review.yml`

The "Review issues" step sets env `MINION_REVIEW_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.minion-review` (line 82) and `DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'false' || inputs.dry_run }}`. Lines 123-147 loop over the issues:
```yaml
          NIGHT=$(date -u +%F)
          ...
            rm -rf "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR"
            if ! minions run .minions/programs/review.md --issue "$ISSUE"; then
              echo "::warning::The review session for #$ISSUE failed. The gate records what it left."
            fi
            if ! go run ./cmd/minion-review gate \
              --issue "$ISSUE" \
              --verdict "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR/verdict.json" \
              --dry-run="$DRY_RUN" \
              --night "$NIGHT"; then
              FAILED="$FAILED #$ISSUE"
            fi
```
`review.md` line 146 writes the verdict to `$MINION_REVIEW_DIR/verdict.json`.

## 5. `cmd/minion-review`

It holds `main.go` and `main_test.go`. The subcommands are `gate`, `dupes` and `next` (switch at lines 53-63). There is no `--mode` flag and no "sweep" mode.

The gate's usage line (line 42):
```go
gateUsage  = "usage: minion-review gate --issue <number> --verdict <path> [--dry-run] [--night YYYY-MM-DD]"
```
The gate itself, lines 82-131:
```go
func gate(args []string) int {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("gate", flag.ContinueOnError)
	var (
		issue   = fs.Int("issue", 0, "reviewed issue number (required)")
		verdict = fs.String("verdict", "", "path to the verdict file (required)")
		dryRun  = fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "record the verdict only; change nothing on the reviewed issue")
		night = fs.String("night", time.Now().UTC().Format(time.DateOnly), "UTC date of the night comment")
	)
	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil { return 2 }
	if *issue <= 0 || *verdict == "" || fs.NArg() > 0 { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, gateUsage); return 2 }
	// --night validated with time.Parse; githubEnv() reads GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_API_URL
	res, err := review.Run(review.Config{
		VerdictPath: *verdict, Repo: repo, Issue: *issue, Night: *night,
		DryRun: *dryRun, APIBaseURL: api, Token: token,
	})
	if err != nil { ...; return 1 }
	if !res.Valid { fmt.Println("minion-review: no verdict:", res.Cause); return 1 }
	mode := ""
	if *dryRun { mode = " (dry run)" }
	fmt.Println("minion-review:", res.Outcome+mode)
	return 0
}
```
Exit codes are 0 for a valid verdict, 1 for no verdict or a GitHub failure, and 2 for a usage or environment error.

## 6. `internal/review`

What each file does:
- **`verdict.go`:** package doc plus the Verdict, Premise and Rewrite types and the outcome/reason constants.
- **`load_verdict.go`:** `LoadVerdict(path string, issue int) (Verdict, error)`. Any error counts as "no verdict".
- **`check_verdict.go`:** `Verdict.check(issue)` and the checks for close, contradiction and rewrite.
- **`rewrite_shape.go`:** `checkShape(oldBody string, rw Rewrite) error`, which checks a rewrite's body shape.
- **`gate.go`:** `Config`, `Result` and `Run`.
- **`act.go`:** `ReviewedLabel`, `buildLabels`, `actable` and `act`, which apply a verdict.
- **`evidence_comment.go`:** `ReviewMarker` and `evidenceComment(v, kept, pulls)`.
- **`row.go`:** builds the tracking rows.
- **`tracking.go`:** tracking issue and night comments (`NightMarker`, `findOrCreateTracking`, `appendRow`, `writeSummary`).
- **`log_summary.go`:** tallies rows and holds `noVerdictLimit` (the "needs you" list).
- **`next.go`:** `Next(gh, NextQuery) ([]int, error)`, which picks the sweep's batch.
- **`list_proposals.go`:** `listProposals`.
- **`dupes.go`, `title_words.go`, `source_refs.go`:** duplicate search (`FindDupes`, `SourceRefs`).

The types and entry point in `gate.go`:
```go
type Config struct {
	VerdictPath string; Repo string; Issue int; Night string
	DryRun bool; APIBaseURL string; Token string; HTTPClient *http.Client
}
type Result struct { Valid bool; Outcome string; Cause string }
func Run(cfg Config) (Result, error)
```
`Run` (gate.go 44-95) works in this order:
1. Reads the issue with `GetIssue`, then `LoadVerdict`.
2. For a rewrite, runs `checkShape`.
3. Outside dry-run, calls `actable` first. A `refusal` becomes no verdict; any other error is returned.
4. Builds `noVerdictRow` or `row`.
5. Calls `act` if the verdict is valid and this is not a dry run.
6. Calls `findOrCreateTracking`, then `appendRow(gh, repo, tracking.Number, cfg.Night, r)`, then `writeSummary`.

No verdict is still recorded as a row, and `Run` returns `Valid=false` with a nil error.

Applying verdicts, from `act.go`:
```go
func actable(gh github.Client, repo string, issue github.Issue, v Verdict) (*github.Issue, error)
func act(gh github.Client, repo string, issue github.Issue, v Verdict, kept *github.Issue) error
```
- **Every outcome:** upserts the evidence comment and adds `minion-reviewed`.
- **Rewrite:** also calls `EditIssue` with the new title and body.
- **Keep or rewrite:** removes whichever of `buildLabels` the issue carries (`minion-approved`, `minion-failed`, `minion-executing`, `do-not-build`).
- **Close:** also calls `CloseIssue`, with "completed" for `ReasonBuilt` and "not_planned" otherwise.

The row format, from `row.go`:
```go
func row(issue github.Issue, v Verdict, dryRun bool) string {
	verdict := "**" + v.Outcome + "**"
	if dryRun { verdict += " (dry run)" }
	line := fmt.Sprintf("- #%d · %s · %s · %s · [link](%s)\n",
		issue.Number, oneLine(issue.Title), verdict, reason(v), issue.HTMLURL)
	...
func noVerdictRow(issue github.Issue, cause string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("- #%d · %s · **no verdict** · %s · [link](%s)\n", ...)
```
The only mode marker in a row is the `" (dry run)"` suffix. There is no "sweep" or "build" field. `log_summary.go`'s `tally.add(key string, dryRun bool)` parses the verdict column, so a new suffix could affect the summary.

## 7. Fake GitHub tests

The package tests live in `internal/review/gate_test.go`, `act_test.go`, `tracking_test.go`, `next_test.go` and `rewrite_shape_test.go`.

The helpers are in `gate_test.go`:
- **`fakeGitHub`** (lines 22-30) holds issues, labels, comments, pulls, `nextID` and `requests []string`.
- **`newFakeGitHub()`** seeds issues #12 and #13.
- **`issueJSON(number, title, body, labels)`** builds an issue.
- **`(f *fakeGitHub) server(t)`** (lines 58-224) is an `http.ServeMux` with routes for issues, labels, comments, pulls and `PATCH issues/comments/{id}`.
- **`trackingIssue(n)`** seeds an existing tracking issue.
- **`writeVerdict(t, json)`** writes a verdict file.
- **`runGate(t, gh, issue, path, night)`** runs a dry run.
- **`runAct(t, gh, issue, path)`** runs for real with night `2026-10-06`.
- **`runGateMode(...)`** calls `Run(Config{..., APIBaseURL: srv.URL, HTTPClient: srv.Client(), DryRun: dryRun})`.
- **`keepVerdict`** is a const verdict string.

The CLI test helper is `fakeGateGitHub(t) *[]string` in `cmd/minion-review/main_test.go` (lines 80-106). `TestGatePassesTheDryRunValue` (lines 109-133) calls `gate([]string{"--issue","12","--verdict",verdict,"--dry-run="+tt.dryRun,"--night","2026-10-06"})` and checks for `POST .../issues/12/labels`.

A representative test, `act_test.go` lines 20-63:
```go
func TestGateKeepActsOnTheIssue(t *testing.T) {
	gh := newFakeGitHub()
	gh.labels = append(gh.labels, ReviewedLabel)
	gh.issues[12] = issueJSON(12, "Add a retry to the pre-push hook", "body",
		[]string{"minion-proposal", "minion-approved", "do-not-build"})
	tracking := gh.trackingIssue(77)

	res := runAct(t, gh, 12, writeVerdict(t, keepVerdict))

	if !res.Valid || res.Outcome != OutcomeKeep {
		t.Fatalf("Result = %+v, want a valid keep", res)
	}
	want := []string{
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12",
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/pulls",
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/labels/minion-reviewed",
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12/comments",
		"POST /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12/comments",
		"DELETE /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12/labels/minion-approved",
		"DELETE /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12/labels/do-not-build",
		"POST /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/12/labels",
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/issues",
		"GET /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/77/comments",
		"POST /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/77/comments",
		"PATCH /repos/partio-io/cli/issues/77",
	}
	if !slices.Equal(gh.requests, want) {
		t.Fatalf("requests:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", strings.Join(gh.requests, "\n"), strings.Join(want, "\n"))
	}
	if got, want := labelNames(gh.issues[12]), []string{"minion-proposal", ReviewedLabel}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("labels = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if got := len(gh.comments[12]); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("reviewed issue has %d comments, want 1", got)
	}
	if gh.issues[12]["state"] != "open" {
		t.Errorf("a keep changed the state to %v", gh.issues[12]["state"])
	}
	row := gh.comments[tracking][0]["body"].(string)
	if !strings.Contains(row, "**keep** ·") || strings.Contains(row, "dry run") {
		t.Errorf("tracking row is not an acted keep:\n%s", row)
	}
}
```
`tracking_test.go` has a `requestsTo(requests, path)` helper and `TestGateNoVerdictWritesRowWithCause` (line 214).

## 8. Premise workflow tests

Both files split the workflow into steps the same way (`repo_build_test.go`):
```go
var workflowStep = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^      - `)
func buildSteps(t *testing.T) []string { return workflowStep.Split(readRepoFile(t, buildWorkflow), -1) }
func stepContaining(steps []string, want string) int   // first step index containing substring, -1 if none
const gateGuard = "steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'"
const researchGuard = "steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'"
```
What `repo_build_test.go` asserts:
- **`TestBuildStageVerifiesBeforeItWritesCode`:** `premise-gate.md` has a `## Context` naming `VerifierPath` and `GatePath`, and `stepContaining(steps,"premise-gate.md") < stepContaining(steps,"minions $ARGS")`.
- **`TestBuildRestatesNeitherVerificationNorGating`** and **`TestBuildStopBehaviourIsTheSameAsResearch`:** content checks on the `premise-gate.md` file.
- **`TestBlockedBuildOpensNoPullRequestAndCreatesNoBranch`:** this is the whole proof of "creates no branch and no pull request". It is structural only: the `minions $ARGS` step must contain `gateGuard`; `premise-gate.md` must not contain `slices: true`; and the program must say "Do not create or modify any file in the working directory" and mention `/tmp`.
- **`TestBlockedBuildNeverClosesTheIssue`:** the program must not contain `gh issue close` or `minion-done`. Each workflow step containing `gh issue close`, `minion-done` or `minion-failed` must contain `gateGuard`.
- **`TestOperatorOverrulesTheBuildByRemovingTheLabel`:** the program must not name `do-not-build`. In the gate step, the index of `minions run .minions/programs/premise-gate.md` must come before the index of `--json labels`.
- **`TestHoldingPremiseLetsTheBuildProceedUnchanged`:** checker phrases, plus the build step's `if:` line must equal exactly `"if: " + gateGuard + " && " + researchGuard`.
- **`TestBuildVerifiesAProposalThatCarriesNoBlock`:** the checker section must contain `NoBlockSection`.

What `repo_chain_test.go` asserts:
- **`TestApprovedIssueIsResearchedBeforeItIsBuilt`:** step order is strictly increasing across these tokens: `"premise-gate.md"`, `"present=true"`, `researchProgramRef` (`.minions/programs/research.md`), `"refusing to build unplanned"`, `"minions $ARGS"`.
- **`TestResearchRunsOnlyWhenTheIssueCarriesNoPlan`:** the research step must contain `if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'`.
- **`TestNoPlanAndNoBlockFailsRatherThanBuildsUnplanned`:** the confirmation step must contain `exit 1`, `BlockingLabel` (`do-not-build`) and `blocked=true`.
- **`TestWorkflowFindsThePlanTheRuntimeFinds`:** extracts `SLICE_PLAN_MARKER: '([^']*)'` and compares it against `runtimePlanMarker` on a table of cases.

## 9. `internal/programshape/repo_workflows_test.go`

`runByAWorkflow` globs `../../.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml` and collects names matching `\.minions/programs/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.md)`. `TestRepoProgramsAreRunByAWorkflow` fails if a program is neither run by a workflow nor listed in the map below. It also fails if a listed program is run, or if a listed program no longer exists.
```go
var manualPrograms = map[string]string{
	"approve.md":       "No workflow runs it.",
	"ingest.md":        "No workflow runs it.",
	"readme-update.md": "No workflow runs it.",
}
```
`TestRepoReviewProgramIsKnown` (line 116) requires that `review.md` is run by a workflow and is not in `manualPrograms`.

A related map, `knownUnreachable` in `repo_programs_test.go`, lists approve, ingest, doc-update and readme-update with reasons.

So once the workflow stops running `premise-gate.md`, you must delete the file or add it to `manualPrograms`. Deleting it also breaks every `gateProgram` read in `repo_build_test.go`.

## 10. Finding the newest PRD and plan comments

Nothing in this repo picks the newest comment. The workflow only runs shell (shown in section 1): `gh issue view --json comments --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"`, which matches the marker in any comment, however old. There is no Go command for it and no notion of a timestamp.

Choosing the latest marked comment happens in the external runtime, partio-minions. The workflow comment cites `internal/slices/slices.go` `planMarkerRe` and `internal/executor/slice.go` `resolveSlicePlan` there.

The comment markers come from `research.md`: the PRD comment starts with `<!-- minion:research run-id=%s -->` (line 510), and the slice comment with `<!-- minion:research-slices parent=#<N> -->` (line 547).

`Makefile` has `lint: golangci-lint run` and nothing else. The config is `.golangci.yml` (v2, enabling errcheck, govet, staticcheck and unused). `checks.yml` and `deadcode-audit.yml` install golangci-lint v2.12.2. There is no actionlint anywhere.

else
            ISSUE_NUM="${{ github.event.issue.number }}"
            echo "path=.minions/programs/implement.md" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "dry_run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "issue_num=${ISSUE_NUM}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi


      - name: Install minions
        run: |
          go install github.com/partio-io/minions/cmd/minions@v0.0.14
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # The premise is checked before the build starts, not inside it. The
      # runtime creates the branch before the agent session runs and pushes
      # unconditionally, so a build that stops partway still leaves a branch
      # and a pull request behind. Stopping here leaves neither.
      - name: Run premise gate
        id: gate
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          minions run .minions/programs/premise-gate.md --issue "$ISSUE_NUM"

          # The gate reports its verdict by labelling the issue — the same
          # signal the approval program already treats as a skip condition.
          # Read the label back rather than the run's exit code: the gate
          # succeeds whether the premise held or not.
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json labels \
              --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qx 'do-not-build'; then
            echo "::notice::Premise does not hold for #${ISSUE_NUM}; skipping the build."
            echo "blocked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "blocked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # A slice plan is the contract between research and the build. The
      # runtime reads the latest comment that carries the marker and builds
      # one slice per session; when no comment carries it, the build falls
      # back to a single unplanned session without a word on the issue
      # (internal/executor/slice.go, resolveSlicePlan). Detect the plan with
      # the pattern the runtime itself uses, so the two never disagree.
      - name: Look for a slice plan
        id: slices
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries a slice plan; research is not needed."
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries no slice plan; research runs first."
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # An approved issue with no slice plan has never been researched.
      # Research it here, in this run, so the build works from a PRD and a
      # slice plan instead of one unplanned session. research.md runs its own
      # premise check and posts the PRD comment, the slice comment and the
      # minion-research-completed label.
      - name: Run research
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          minions run .minions/programs/research.md --issue "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"

      # research.md produces no slice plan when its own premise-checker blocks
      # the run. Without this step the build would fall back to the single
      # unplanned session that this chain exists to remove, so the plan is
      # confirmed before the build is allowed to start.
      - name: Confirm research produced a slice plan
        id: researched
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "blocked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # research.md's premise-checker applies stage-gate.md, which labels
          # the issue do-not-build. That is a block, not a failure: the gate
          # has already posted the comment that explains it.
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json labels \
              --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qx 'do-not-build'; then
            echo "::notice::Research blocked the premise for #${ISSUE_NUM}; skipping the build."
            echo "blocked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "::error::Research produced no slice plan for #${ISSUE_NUM} and did not block the premise; refusing to build unplanned."
          exit 1

      - name: Run program
        if: steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ARGS="run ${{ steps.program.outputs.path }}"
          if [ -n "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}" ]; then
            ARGS="${ARGS} --issue ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          fi
          if [ "${{ steps.program.outputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            ARGS="${ARGS} --dry-run"
          fi
          minions $ARGS

      # A blocked run is not a completion and not a failure. Either gate can
      # block it: the premise gate above, or research's own premise-checker.
      # Both of the steps below are skipped so the blocking gate's comment
      # stays the only account of what happened, and the issue is neither
      # closed nor marked failed.
      - name: Mark done
        if: success() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          # Find the PR this run opened. The branch name is deterministic per
          # issue, so we can locate the PR without the agent reporting it.
          PR=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" \
            --head "minion/implement-implement-${ISSUE_NUM}" \
            --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          # A "successful" run that produced no PR is a silent failure, not a
          # completion. Fail red instead of closing the issue with no work done.
          if [ -z "$PR" ]; then
            echo "::error::Program succeeded but no PR exists for #${ISSUE_NUM}; refusing to mark done."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Keep the PR and issue linked. implement.md asks the agent to add a
          # "Closes #N" reference but it does not do so reliably, so enforce it.
          if ! gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body' \
              | grep -qE "#${ISSUE_NUM}([^0-9]|$)"; then
            BODY=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body')
            gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --body "${BODY}"$'\n\n'"Closes #${ISSUE_NUM}"
          fi

          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" \
            --add-label "minion-done" --remove-label "minion-executing"
          gh issue close "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" \
            --comment "Minion completed — see PR #${PR}."

      - name: Mark failed
        if: failure() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          RUN_URL="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --add-label "minion-failed" --remove-label "minion-executing"
          gh issue comment "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --body "Minion execution failed. [View logs](${RUN_URL})"
---

target_repos:

# Proposal review

Judge one proposal issue, and write the judgment as a verdict file. This
program writes no code and opens no pull request. A gate reads the
verdict after this session ends, and only the gate records it.

A proposal can be wrong in ways its author could not see when it was
filed. Its premise can be false today, the idea can be built already, or
it can describe a feature this project has no use for. Issue #30 reached
three builds on a false premise. A review catches that before a build
spends anything on it.

## Context

- `cli/.minions/premise-verifier.md`
- `cli/.minions/ingest-prompt.md`

      # (internal/executor/slice.go, resolveSlicePlan). Detect the plan with
      # the pattern the runtime itself uses, so the two never disagree.
      - name: Look for a slice plan
        id: slices
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries a slice plan; research is not needed."
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::notice::#${ISSUE_NUM} carries no slice plan; research runs first."
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # An approved issue with no slice plan has never been researched.
      # Research it here, in this run, so the build works from a PRD and a
      # slice plan instead of one unplanned session. research.md runs its own
      # premise check and posts the PRD comment, the slice comment and the
      # minion-research-completed label.
      - name: Run research
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          minions run .minions/programs/research.md --issue "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"

      # research.md produces no slice plan when its own premise-checker blocks
      # the run. Without this step the build would fall back to the single
      # unplanned session that this chain exists to remove, so the plan is
      # confirmed before the build is allowed to start.
      - name: Confirm research produced a slice plan
        id: researched
        if: steps.slices.outputs.present == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
              --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -qE "$SLICE_PLAN_MARKER"; then
            echo "blocked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # research.md's premise-checker applies stage-gate.md, which labels
          # the issue do-not-build. That is a block, not a failure: the gate
          # has already posted the comment that explains it.
          if gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" --json labels \
              --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qx 'do-not-build'; then
            echo "::notice::Research blocked the premise for #${ISSUE_NUM}; skipping the build."
            echo "blocked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "::error::Research produced no slice plan for #${ISSUE_NUM} and did not block the premise; refusing to build unplanned."
          exit 1

      - name: Run program
        if: steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ARGS="run ${{ steps.program.outputs.path }}"
          if [ -n "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}" ]; then
            ARGS="${ARGS} --issue ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          fi
          if [ "${{ steps.program.outputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            ARGS="${ARGS} --dry-run"
          fi
          minions $ARGS

      # A blocked run is not a completion and not a failure. Either gate can
      # block it: the premise gate above, or research's own premise-checker.
      # Both of the steps below are skipped so the blocking gate's comment
      # stays the only account of what happened, and the issue is neither
      # closed nor marked failed.
      - name: Mark done
        if: success() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          # Find the PR this run opened. The branch name is deterministic per
          # issue, so we can locate the PR without the agent reporting it.
          PR=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" \
            --head "minion/implement-implement-${ISSUE_NUM}" \
            --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          # A "successful" run that produced no PR is a silent failure, not a
          # completion. Fail red instead of closing the issue with no work done.
          if [ -z "$PR" ]; then
            echo "::error::Program succeeded but no PR exists for #${ISSUE_NUM}; refusing to mark done."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Keep the PR and issue linked. implement.md asks the agent to add a
          # "Closes #N" reference but it does not do so reliably, so enforce it.
          if ! gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body' \
              | grep -qE "#${ISSUE_NUM}([^0-9]|$)"; then
            BODY=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body')
            gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --body "${BODY}"$'\n\n'"Closes #${ISSUE_NUM}"
          fi

          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" \
            --add-label "minion-done" --remove-label "minion-executing"
          gh issue close "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "$REPO" \
            --comment "Minion completed — see PR #${PR}."

      - name: Mark failed
        if: failure() && steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true' && steps.researched.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"
          RUN_URL="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --add-label "minion-failed" --remove-label "minion-executing"
          gh issue comment "$ISSUE_NUM" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --body "Minion execution failed. [View logs](${RUN_URL})"
---
id: review
target_repos:
  - cli
---

# Proposal review

Judge one proposal issue, and write the judgment as a verdict file. This
program writes no code and opens no pull request. A gate reads the
verdict after this session ends, and only the gate records it.

A proposal can be wrong in ways its author could not see when it was
filed. Its premise can be false today, the idea can be built already, or
it can describe a feature this project has no use for. Issue #30 reached
three builds on a false premise. A review catches that before a build
spends anything on it.

- `cli/.minions/premise-verifier.md`
- `cli/.minions/ingest-prompt.md`

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      program:
        description: "Program .md file path (e.g., .minions/programs/detect-hooks.md)"
        required: true
        type: string

    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && (github.event.label.name == 'minion-ready' || github.event.label.name == 'minion-approved')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '/minion build'))
    runs-on: github-runner-partio-minion-ai-01
    timeout-minutes: 180

    env:
